name: Unsupported claim about Edgar
definition: The reply states something about Edgar that career.md does not support. This includes treating absence as a negative (not mentioned, so not done) and presenting a typical or industry figure as Edgar's own.
pass: Claims traceable to career.md; a general figure explicitly framed as typical and not about Edgar
fail: States something about Edgar the record does not support, including "not mentioned, so not done" (absence as negative) and a typical/industry figure presented as Edgar's own

name: Wordy decline
definition: An out-of-scope request (general chat, persona, trivia) gets a decline padded with facts about Edgar, employer lists or several offers, which costs tokens and adds nothing.
pass: One or two short sentences: decline + what the bot is for
fail: Out-of-scope request (general chat, persona, trivia) gets more than a one-line decline plus the bot's purpose: extra facts about Edgar, employer lists, multiple offers

name: Needless gap statement
definition: An in-scope reply volunteers what the record does not cover when the visitor did not ask for that fact.
pass: Saying the record lacks a fact the visitor asked for directly; listing honest gaps from the record when relevant
fail: Volunteers what the record does not cover when the visitor did not ask for that fact

name: Contacts on off-topic requests
definition: The reply points to the contact buttons on a request that has nothing to do with Edgar.
pass: Contacts offered when the visitor wants to reach Edgar, including after a "not a match" fit answer
fail: Points to the contact buttons on a request unrelated to Edgar

name: Gap in the career file
definition: A fact Edgar wants the bot to answer is missing from career.md, so the fix is a corpus edit rather than a prompt change.
fail: A fact Edgar wants answered is missing from career.md

name: Empty reply
definition: The visible reply is empty, even when a fallback shows the contact buttons.

name: Repeated sentence
definition: The same fact or sentence is stated twice in one reply.
fail: The same fact or sentence stated twice in one reply

name: Mixed language
definition: A reply mixes languages: English sentences in a reply to Russian input, or the reverse, beyond names, titles, product names and URLs.
pass: Single reply language per the language rule
fail: A Russian-input reply contains English sentences (or vice versa for English input) beyond names, titles, product names and URLs

name: Cut-off reply
definition: The reply stops at the output token limit mid-sentence.
fail: The reply stops at the token limit mid-sentence
